minutes.headline: Planning Board approved two ANR plans and a common driveway, and released the Emerald Place bond.
minutes.summary: The board approved an ANR plan for 322 Flat Hill Road, then an ANR plan and a common driveway for 335 Chase Road. It voted to release the surety for Emerald Place at Lake Wayland. Most of the meeting went to shaping a solar bylaw survey, with further talk of a model open space bylaw, the master plan and public outreach on Earth removal.

attendees.role: presenter, professional land surveyor with Hannigan engineering

votes.motion: Approve the ANR plan as submitted for 322 Flat Hill Road
Separate motion to notify other land use boards of the withdrawal from Chapter land
Approve the ANR plan for 335 Chase Road
Approve the proposed common driveway at 335 Chase Road, with the stipulation that the existing fieldstone wall be retained
Release the surety for Emerald Place at Lake Wayland

decisions.decision: The Rob's Hill Road and Sunset Lane common drive was put off to January so all four members can hear it.
Solar survey questions reordered: vegetative buffer questions and an acreage-versus-size question added, a small-system size question offered in tiers, and the fencing question removed.
Staff will send a short letter or email to the town manager and Select Board chair to coordinate master plan work on population projections and facilities.
Prior minutes were tabled until the amendments can be discussed with the member who proposed them.
Staff will bring an Earth-removal-only bylaw draft to the first January meeting, with public information sessions planned for February.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board approved an ANR plan for 335 Chase Road and a common driveway there, on the condition that the existing fieldstone wall be kept.
The board voted to release the surety for Emerald Place at Lake Wayland.
The board approved an ANR plan as submitted for 322 Flat Hill Road.
The Rob's Hill Road and Sunset Lane common drive was put off to January so all four members can hear it.
Staff will bring an Earth-removal-only bylaw draft to the first January meeting, with public information sessions planned for February.

why_it_matters: The Earth-removal bylaw is the item most likely to reach residents, since a draft and public sessions are planned and any bylaw would later go to a Town Meeting vote.
The solar survey questions and the master plan coordination with the Select Board shape later land-use rules and town facility planning, though no vote on either was taken.
